prompt: Best airline-approved power bank that can charge a laptop on a plane
queries: best power bank for laptop airline approved under 100Wh 2026
airlines banning power bank use in flight 2026 rules
answer:
**Short answer:** Get a power bank rated under 100Wh with at least 65–100W USB-C PD output. My top pick is the **Anker Prime 27,650mAh (250W)**. It has the highest output of the options I found, at about 99.5Wh. The catch is that some airlines now ban using a power bank in flight at all, so check your airline's rules first.

**Options (all under 100Wh, from retailer and brand pages, so check the Wh label on the unit):**
- **Anker Prime 27,650mAh (250W):** about 99.5Wh, 140W per port, 650g. It has the most power, but it is heavy and sits right at the limit.
- **INIU B64:** about 99.9Wh, 140W, 624g. It is also right at the limit.
- **CUKTECH 20:** about 90Wh, 140W per port. It has more margin under the limit.
- **UGREEN 145W:** about 90Wh, 100W per port, 513g. It is the lightest of the high-output options.
- **Belkin BoostCharge Pro 20K:** about 74Wh, 100W in and out. It is the budget option and can charge a 14" MacBook Pro.

**Which to pick:**
- For a typical laptop, a 65–100W port is enough, so the UGREEN or CUKTECH is the best balance.
- For a gaming laptop or a 16" MacBook Pro, get the Anker Prime or INIU.
- For an ultrabook or MacBook Air, the Belkin is plenty.

**Airline rules:**
- The standard rule is that power banks under 100Wh are allowed in carry-on only. Banks of 100–160Wh need airline approval, and anything over 160Wh is banned.
- Some airlines now restrict use in flight. Since 15 Jan 2026, Lufthansa, SWISS and Austrian don't allow power banks to be used or charged on board. They also cap you at two power banks per passenger and don't allow them in overhead bins. A retailer blog claims a similar ICAO rule, but I couldn't confirm it from an official source.
- I found no blanket ban from other major airlines, but rules vary by carrier. If your airline bans in-flight use, no power bank will charge your laptop on that flight. In that case, use the seat power outlet instead.

Look up your airline's policy before you fly, and keep the bank in your carry-on, not checked baggage.
